I visited Madhu Agarwal Maternity & Nursing Home (Bhayander West) after seeing their high rating and number of positive reviews — but unfortunately, my experience was extremely disappointing.

After visiting, I realized that most of those 5-star reviews are not genuine. The doctors themselves take patients’ phones and post positive reviews, which is highly unethical. Both Dr. Madhu Agarwal and Dr. Nikita Agarwal seem to be completely money-minded, with little concern for patient care.

Dr. Nikita Agarwal in particular is extremely rude — not just to patients, but even to their family members. Several genuine reviews also mention the same, and I can now confirm it’s true.

Surprisingly, being a maternity hospital, they appear to have little patience or affection for babies. They don’t allow small children in the consultation room and even scold parents for holding their baby’s hand.

On top of that, their charges are exorbitant:

UPT kit costing ₹100 elsewhere is billed at ₹500, CBC ₹500, Ultrasonography ₹3000+ (recommended multiple times unnecessarily)

Medicines sold at inflated rates — items worth ₹60 charged in thousands.

These rates are far higher than what other maternity centers charge in the area.

I can already predict their response — they usually give the same copy-paste reply to every genuine review. But I’m writing this so that others don’t fall into the same trap.

I sincerely hope authorities take note of such unethical practices, review their license, and take strict action.

( shows how reliable their own staff is)

Instead of clarifying the miscommunication with their own staff, the doctor ends up shouting at patients, which is extremely unprofessional.

The pricing is another serious concern. Medicines are sold at heavily inflated prices. On top of that, no proper bill has been provided for any medicines given or for any sonogram conducted so far.

To make things worse, there is no consistency in charges. The same routine procedure is billed differently on different visits. It feels like they are unsure how much to charge and decide arbitrarily each time.

Overall, the experience felt unprofessional and lacking in transparency. I’m sharing this so that others can make an informed decision before choosing this hospital. I genuinely hope stricter monitoring is done to ensure ethical medical practices and fair billing.

Worst Experience for Pregnancy & Delivery
We had a very disappointing and traumatic experience at this hospital during pregnancy delivery.
Our newborn was admitted to the NICU for 2 days with the explanation that the baby had “eaten potty,” cried late, and was separated from the mother immediately after birth. During this critical time, the baby was kept away from the mother for two full days, which caused unnecessary stress and anxiety for our family.
What was most concerning is that breastfeeding (mother’s milk) was not encouraged initially, despite it being essential for a newborn’s recovery. Only after Dr. Pareeniti — the only doctor who showed genuine care and responsibility — strongly insisted on mother’s milk, the pediatrician finally discharged our baby from the NICU.
This raises serious questions about:
Unnecessary NICU admission
Poor coordination between doctors
Lack of emotional support for the mother
Keeping a newborn away from the mother without proper justification
We are thankful to Dr. Pareeniti for her ethical approach and concern; otherwise, our baby might have stayed in NICU longer without real need.
Overall, this was a very bad experience, and we would not recommend this hospital for pregnancy or delivery care. New parents deserve transparency, empathy, and medically sound decisions — sadly, we did not receive that here.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Kind att TPA TEAM
MIRA MULTISPECIALITY HOSPITAL.
BHAYANDAR WEST

I am extremely disappointed with the TPA service at Mira Multispeciality Hospital. A very similar issue had already happened earlier with one of my relatives, where the TPA team was repeatedly instructed nearly five times to scan and submit the doctor’s first prescription along with the required documents to the mediclaim company. Despite repeated reminders, they failed to do so, and because of their negligence, the claim was rejected.

Now the exact same mistake has happened again in my mother’s case while I am currently at the hospital. The physician had clearly prescribed and documented her medical condition, but the TPA team again failed to send the doctor’s initial prescription and proper documents to the insurance company on time. Because of this negligence, a query was raised by the mediclaim company asking for additional clarification and documents.

Even after the query was raised, the response from the TPA department was extremely casual. They simply said that it would take more time and that they could not process it immediately. Shockingly, they finally applied for the approval only around 5:00 PM on Saturday evening, fully aware that Sunday is a non-working day for many insurance processing departments. Due to this delay, the entire approval process has now been unnecessarily pushed ahead.

This does not look like a small accidental mistake anymore. When the same negligence happens repeatedly in multiple cases, it naturally creates doubt that these delays are being done intentionally so that the hospital billing cycle increases and patients are forced to stay longer, resulting in additional financial burden.

My mother is medically fit right now and ready for discharge. If the TPA team had submitted the doctor’s prescription and documents properly and on time, there would most likely have been no unnecessary query from the insurance company, and the mediclaim process would have been completed smoothly without any issue.

Because of this delay, my entire travel plan is now at risk. My mother has a flight scheduled on Monday, and if discharge gets delayed until sunday afternoon, it will become extremely difficult for us to reach the airport on time. If we miss the flight, I may suffer a loss of nearly ₹40,000. The question is — who will bear this loss caused purely due to the negligence and delay from the TPA department?

I am financially capable of managing this situation somehow, but I genuinely feel worried thinking about what ordinary families might go through in such situations. Many people may not have the financial strength, resources, or confidence to handle this kind of unnecessary stress and delay.

Money is not everything. Hospitals and TPA teams are dealing with patients and families during emotionally difficult times. Basic responsibility, honesty, and humanity are expected. I sincerely request the concerned people to fear God and understand the impact of their actions on patients and families.

As Lord Krishna teaches, every person’s time eventually comes, and whatever we do in this world must ultimately be faced and repaid here itself. We live our lives with this belief and understanding.

God sees everything. 🙏🙏

" jay shree krishna "
